responses.polygon: A polygon is a closed 2D shape bounded by three or more straight line segments.
responses.triangle_sides: A triangle has three sides and interior angles that sum to 180°.
responses.quadrilateral_sides: A quadrilateral is a four-sided polygon with interior angles summing to 360°.
responses.pi: Pi (π) is the mathematical constant representing the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, approximately equal to 3.14159.
responses.prime_number: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself (e.g., 2, 3, 5, 7, 11).
responses.pythagorean_theorem: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (c) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides (a and b): a² + b² = c².
responses.quadratic_formula: The quadratic formula solves ax² + bx + c = 0 as x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a).
responses.mean_median_mode: Mean is the numerical average, median is the middle value when sorted, and mode is the most frequently occurring value in a dataset.
responses.calculus: Calculus is the branch of mathematics studying continuous change, divided into differential calculus (rates of change) and integral calculus (accumulation of quantities).
responses.matrix: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers, symbols, or expressions arranged in rows and columns.
responses.physics: Physics is the branch of natural science that studies matter, energy, motion, and the fundamental forces of the universe.
responses.force: Force is an interaction that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body (Force = mass × acceleration). Its SI unit is the Newton (N).
responses.velocity: Velocity is a vector quantity representing the rate of change of displacement over time in a specified direction.
responses.acceleration: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity per unit time (a = (v - u) / t).
responses.gravity: Gravity is the fundamental attractive force exerted between any two masses in the universe, described by Newton's law of universal gravitation and General Relativity.
responses.kinetic_energy: Kinetic energy is the energy an object possesses due to its motion: Ek = ½mv².
responses.potential_energy: Potential energy is stored energy an object possesses due to its position or configuration in a field: Ep = mgh.
responses.friction: Friction is the contact force that opposes relative motion between two touching surfaces.
responses.density: Density is mass per unit volume of a substance (Density = Mass / Volume), measured in kg/m³ or g/cm³.
responses.ohms_law: Ohm's Law states that current (I) flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to voltage (V) across them and inversely proportional to resistance (R): V = IR.
responses.newtons_laws: Newton's Laws of Motion describe object dynamics: 1) Inertia, 2) F = ma, and 3) Action and reaction are equal and opposite.
responses.si_units: The International System of Units (SI) relies on seven defining fundamental physical constants, including the Planck constant (h), elementary charge (e), and speed of light (c).
responses.work_energy_power: Work is energy transferred by a force acting through distance (W = Fd), and Power is the rate of doing work (P = W / t), measured in Watts (W).
responses.chemistry: Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties, composition, structure, and chemical reactions of matter.
responses.branches_chemistry: Main branches include Organic, Inorganic, Physical, Analytical Chemistry, and Biochemistry.
responses.matter: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies volume (space).
responses.states_of_matter: The fundamental states of matter are solid, liquid, gas, and plasma.
responses.solid: Solids have a fixed volume and rigid shape because constituent particles are closely packed in fixed positions.
responses.liquid: Liquids have a definite volume but assume the shape of their container because particles can flow past one another.
responses.gas: Gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume, expanding freely to fill available space.
responses.atom: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element that retains the chemical identity of that element.
responses.subatomic_particles: The main subatomic particles are positively charged protons and uncharged neutrons in the nucleus, and negatively charged electrons in surrounding orbitals.
responses.periodic_table: The periodic table organizes elements by increasing atomic number (Z), grouping elements with similar electron configurations and chemical trends.
responses.acid: An acid is a proton donor (H⁺ donor) that turns blue litmus red and has a pH below 7 in aqueous solutions.
responses.base: A base (or alkali when soluble) is a proton acceptor (H⁺ acceptor or OH⁻ producer) that turns red litmus blue and has a pH above 7.
responses.neutralization: Neutralization is the reaction between an acid and a base producing a salt and water (Acid + Base → Salt + Water).
responses.mole_concept: A mole is the SI unit of amount of substance, containing exactly 6.02214076 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's constant).
responses.chemical_bonding: Chemical bonding includes covalent bonding (shared electron pairs), ionic bonding (electrostatic attraction between ions), and metallic bonding.
responses.living_things: Living organisms are characterized by vital processes: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity (Irritability), Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, and Nutrition (MR NIGER D).
responses.cell: A cell is the fundamental structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms.
responses.tissue: A tissue is a group of similar cells specialized to perform a specific function (e.g., epithelial, muscular, xylem).
responses.organ: An organ is a structure composed of distinct tissues working together to perform specialized functions (e.g., heart, leaf).
responses.organ_system: An organ system is a group of organs that collaborate to carry out complex body functions (e.g., digestive system).
responses.taxonomic_groups: The hierarchical biological classification ranks are Domain, Kingdom, Phylum (or Division), Class, Order, Family, Genus, and Species.
responses.species: A species is the basic unit of biological classification, defining organisms capable of interbreeding to produce fertile offspring.
responses.five_kingdoms: The traditional five-kingdom classification system comprises Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
responses.carbohydrates: Carbohydrates are organic molecules made of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen that serve as primary metabolic energy sources.
responses.proteins: Proteins are polymers made of amino acid chains required for structural support, tissue repair, enzymes, and cell signaling.
responses.lipids: Lipids (fats and oils) function as long-term energy reserves, structural components of cell membranes, and thermal insulation.
responses.enzymes: Enzymes are biological catalysts (protein molecules) that speed up metabolic reactions without being consumed in the process.
responses.photosynthesis: Photosynthesis is the process where green plants use sunlight energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen (6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂).
responses.osmosis: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water potential to lower water potential.
responses.dna: DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) is the double-helical molecule carrying genetic instructions for the development, function, and reproduction of living organisms.
responses.genetics: Genetics is the scientific study of heredity, genes, and variation in living organisms.
responses.computer: A computer is an electronic device that accepts raw data, processes it according to stored instructions, and produces meaningful output.
responses.algorithm: An algorithm is an explicit, step-by-step procedure or set of rules designed to solve a problem or perform a task.
responses.variable: A variable is a named memory location in code that holds data values that can change during program execution.
responses.function: A function is a self-contained, reusable block of code designed to execute a specific task when called.
responses.loop: A loop is a control flow construct that repeatedly executes a block of code while a specified condition holds true.
responses.database: A database is an organized collection of structured data stored and managed electronically using a DBMS (Database Management System).
responses.operating_system: An operating system (OS) is essential system software managing computer hardware resources and providing core services for application software.
responses.python: Python is an interpreted, high-level, general-purpose programming language noted for its readable syntax, rich ecosystem, and versatility.
responses.cpu: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the primary hardware component that executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logical processing.
responses.ai_ml: Artificial Intelligence (AI) enables machines to perform tasks requiring intelligence; Machine Learning (ML) is a subfield focused on learning patterns from data.
responses.cybersecurity: Cybersecurity encompasses practices, technologies, and processes designed to protect systems, networks, and data from digital attacks or unauthorized access.
responses.agriculture: Agriculture is the science, art, and business of soil cultivation, crop production, and livestock management for human consumption and commercial use.
responses.mechanisation: Agricultural mechanization involves introducing mechanical power and modern machinery (tractors, harvesters) to increase farming productivity.
responses.simple_tools: Simple farm tools include hand-operated implements like cutlasses, hoes, spades, rakes, and watering cans.
responses.cutlass: A cutlass is a versatile hand tool used for clearing bush, cutting vegetation, and harvesting root crops.
responses.hoe: A hoe is a manual cultivation tool used for weeding, turning topsoil, making ridges, and harvesting.
responses.tractor: A tractor is a heavy-duty motor vehicle engineered to supply mechanical power for agricultural implements like ploughs and seeders.
responses.plough: A plough is a primary tillage implement used to break up, overturn, and aerate soil prior to planting.
responses.harrow: A harrow is a secondary tillage tool used to pulverize heavy soil clods, level the field, and clear weeds.
responses.crop_rotation: Crop rotation is the systematic practice of growing different crop species in recurrent succession on the same land to maintain soil fertility and break pest cycles.
responses.irrigation: Irrigation is the artificial application of controlled amounts of water to agricultural land to support crop growth during dry periods.
responses.geography: Geography is the study of Earth's physical environments, human societies, spatial relationships, and environmental interactions.
responses.equator: The Equator is an imaginary line encircling Earth at 0° latitude, dividing it into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
responses.continent: A continent is one of Earth's seven largest continuous landmasses: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.
responses.latitude: Latitude measures angular distance north or south from the Equator (0° to 90° N/S).
responses.longitude: Longitude measures angular distance east or west from the Prime Meridian at Greenwich (0° to 180° E/W).
responses.atmosphere: The atmosphere is the envelope of gases surrounding Earth, predominantly composed of nitrogen (78%) and oxygen (21%).
responses.plate_tectonics: Plate tectonics is the scientific theory explaining the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates, causing earthquakes, mountain formation, and volcanism.
responses.weather_vs_climate: Weather describes short-term atmospheric conditions in a specific area, whereas climate is the long-term average weather pattern over 30+ years.
responses.economics: Economics is the social science analyzing the allocation of scarce resources toward fulfilling unlimited human wants.
responses.supply_demand: The law of supply and demand governs market pricing: prices rise when demand exceeds supply and fall when supply exceeds demand.
responses.inflation: Inflation represents a sustained, general increase in price levels across an economy, eroding purchasing power over time.
responses.market: A market is any institutional arrangement facilitating interactions between buyers and sellers to exchange goods, services, or information.
responses.gdp: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country over a specific time period.
responses.capital: Capital refers to accumulated wealth, machinery, tools, and financial assets used to generate further income or produce goods.
responses.government: Government is the political organization or system through which a state or nation is governed and administered.
responses.constitution: A constitution is the supreme legal framework detailing the fundamental laws, rights, and principles governing a nation.
responses.democracy: Democracy is a system of government where supreme political authority is held and exercised by the general population through free elections.
responses.branches_government: The three branches of government are the Legislature (enacts laws), Executive (enforces laws), and Judiciary (adjudicates laws).
responses.citizenship: Citizenship represents legal membership in a sovereign state, conferring rights, duties, and civic obligations.
responses.lamb_of_god: John the Baptist identified Jesus Christ as the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29).
responses.darkness: In biblical contexts, darkness represents sin, spiritual blindness, evil, and alienation from God.
responses.faith: Faith is defined in Hebrews 11:1 as the assurance of things hoped for and the conviction of things not seen.
responses.grace: Grace refers to God's unearned, divine favor and mercy extended toward humanity.
responses.ten_commandments: The Ten Commandments are divine moral laws delivered to Moses on Mount Sinai (Exodus 20).
